subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: When a legacy BLOB and TEXT primary-key value normalize to the same canonical TEXT key, should the migration fail without data loss or discard one row automatically?
rationale: This is an irreversible persisted-state and availability trade-off; the PR body and current-head commit message describe different outcomes, so reviewer inference cannot safely establish the intended upgrade contract.

options.title: Fail on normalization collisions
options.body: Preserve both legacy rows and stop with a clear doctor-guided recovery message when normalization would collapse distinct stored values.

options.title: Keep canonical TEXT automatically
options.body: Discard the colliding BLOB-keyed row during migration and explicitly accept that this upgrade may lose one persisted record.

recommendation.title: Fail on normalization collisions
recommendation.body: Preserve both legacy rows and stop with a clear doctor-guided recovery message when normalization would collapse distinct stored values.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged STRICT-migration implementation establishes the storage-invariant and upgrade-policy boundary involved here.
